desk.headline: Continuing HEPS up 16% to 30.3c as operating income rises 10% to R2.57bn; interim dividend flat at 24c; outlook positive but cautious

other.label: Operating income (revenue net of direct expenses)

results: Operating income rose 10% to R2.57bn and normalised operating profit 17% to R521m, as costs grew more slowly than income.
HEPS from continuing operations rose 16% to 30.3c; total HEPS fell 9% because last year included a once-off gain from the old ETV matter.
All four divisions grew: Investments up 16% to R870m, Retail up 15% to R421m, Corporate up 6% to R1.02bn and Growth markets up 3% to R233m.
Assets under administration and management rose 13% to R784.5bn, and the Investments division had R20.9bn of positive net flows.
The interim dividend was kept at 24c; the stake in TSA Administration was raised to 80% from 60%.

guidance.summary: No earnings targets. The board sees the first half as a solid base for the year and expects organic growth in core businesses, while calling the operating environment uncertain. The planned buyback of about 28.7% of shares from New Veld, still subject to conditions, is expected to boost earnings per share once done.

points: CEO Dawie de Villiers credited a sharper focus on clients and a tighter connected value chain for the growth.
He highlighted significant technology projects won in South Africa, Botswana and Namibia.
He wants to make the group's investment skills available to individual investors, through unit trusts, active ETFs and digital channels.
Management said the New Veld buyback lets it buy a large block of shares at a price the independent directors see as attractive.
call.source: CEO statement in the results announcement, and Business Day and The National coverage (26 Nov 2026)

watch: Completion of the R6.75-a-share buyback of about 372.8 million shares from New Veld and the resulting rise in ARC's stake to about 78%.
Whether cost growth stays below income growth as technology spending continues.
New business flows into the Investments and Retail divisions.
